findings.title: Unauthenticated tenant selection makes session UUIDs non-capabilities
findings.evidence: SPEC-06 tenant resolver: `if (ctx.Request.Query.TryGetValue("tenant", out var t) ... return t!;` and fallback `return _options.DefaultTenantId;`. SPEC-06 §4.2 exposes `GET /api/dhf/sessions` for the resolved tenant. SPEC-00 SDR-TL-012 claims viewer access control is `knowledge of the session UUID` and that exposure requires `accidentally sharing a URL`.
findings.problem: The public viewer can list session IDs for `default` or any caller-supplied `?tenant=` value without knowing a session UUID first. That invalidates the stated URL-as-capability model.
findings.why_it_matters: Anyone who can hit the viewer can enumerate session metadata and obtain session IDs, so the UUID is no longer the access secret. This is a direct confidentiality break, not just a documentation issue.
findings.proposed_fix: For v1, remove unauthenticated session listing and tenant override from the public surface. Require a session-specific capability token to fetch a single session, or add real auth before exposing `/api/dhf/sessions` and `/` session lists.

findings.title: Mandatory recovery events have no storage or hash-chain representation
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam B, Seam C, §6 Glossary; SPEC-04 §3.1, §5, §9.1
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 glossary: `Recovery Event: A DHF entry (distinct from a turn entry) ... Appended via DhfLedger.AppendRecoveryEventAsync. Participates in the hash chain.` SPEC-04 exposes `AppendRecoveryEventAsync(...)` in `IDhfRepository`, but `dhf.entries.turn_type` only allows `('execution', 'clarification', 'confirmation', 'ambiguity_resolution')`, and no recovery-event table or row shape is defined.
findings.problem: The spec makes recovery-event logging mandatory, but never defines how a recovery event is stored, hashed, sequenced, or read back.
findings.why_it_matters: Post-timeout and post-crash recovery is a never-descoped safety mechanism in this bundle. Without a concrete persisted representation, that mechanism cannot be implemented or verified.
findings.proposed_fix: Define one authoritative persistence model for recovery events: either add a recovery-compatible entry kind to `dhf.entries` plus hash rules, or add a separate chained `dhf.recovery_events` table and update repository/read contracts accordingly.

findings.title: Screenshot bytes required by validation and viewer are not stored in the DHF schema
findings.evidence: `dhf.entries` stores only `screenshot_before_path`, `screenshot_after_path`, `screenshot_before_sha256`, `screenshot_after_sha256`. SPEC-04 §10.2 says `In v1 deployment, screenshots are stored inline in DHF as screenshot_png bytea`. SPEC-06 §5.2 says entry detail returns inline screenshot `dataUrl` content. SPEC-04 read-side `EntryDetail` contains only screenshot SHA-256 fields, not bytes, URLs, or S3 keys.
findings.problem: The schema and read DTOs do not contain the screenshot payload that deep validation and the viewer claim to consume.
findings.why_it_matters: Deep hash validation of screenshots and viewer screenshot rendering are impossible from the documented schema. This is an implementation blocker, not a missing detail.
findings.proposed_fix: Add explicit screenshot storage to SPEC-04 schema and read contracts (e.g. bytea columns or a separate artifact table with S3 key/bytes metadata), or remove screenshot replay/validation from v1 scope everywhere it is currently promised.

findings.title: Session lock on DHF append failure is not durable across orchestrator restart
findings.location: SPEC-00 Seam C; SPEC-04 §11 DHF-014; SPEC-00 changelog/glossary on session survival across orchestrator restart
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 Seam C: `Reopening requires manual intervention`. SPEC-04 DHF-014 says `The session is marked locked in memory`. SPEC-00 changelog/glossary explicitly preserves sessions across orchestrator restart.
findings.problem: The lock state exists only in process memory, but the session survives process restart. A restart clears the lock and allows the same persisted session to continue without the required manual intervention.
findings.why_it_matters: This defeats the safety barrier meant to stop further writes after an audit-path failure. Railway restarts are part of the stated deployment model, so this is not an edge case.
findings.proposed_fix: Persist lock state in the database (`locked_at`, `lock_reason`, `locked_by_failure`) and enforce it in `OpenOrResumeSessionAsync` and `AppendTurnAsync`. Do not rely on in-memory state for a persisted-session invariant.

findings.title: `IReadOnlyDhfRepository.ValidateChainAsync` is side-effectful in deep mode
findings.evidence: SPEC-06 SDR-06-003: `The viewer never writes to any table. All paths go through IReadOnlyDhfRepository`. SPEC-04 §10.2: `Deep validation writes integrity_event decorations for detected failures via WriteIntegrityEventAsync`.
findings.problem: The read-only repository contract is presented as non-writing, but one of its exposed methods performs writes in deep mode.
findings.why_it_matters: This breaks the core isolation guarantee for the viewer and makes a GET-style integrity check mutate the audit log. It also invalidates the claim that the viewer has no write paths.
findings.proposed_fix: Make `ValidateChainAsync` side-effect-free for `IReadOnlyDhfRepository`. If persistence of integrity findings is required, move it to a separate write-capable service or an explicit admin/orchestrator path.

findings.title: `explicit_shutdown` closure reason is not implementable from the defined wire contract
findings.evidence: SPEC-00 glossary defines `explicit_shutdown` as `add-in sends a teardown message or the orchestrator detects add-in disconnect`. The same paragraph later says `SPEC-02 must emit an explicit teardown message before process exit` if finer-grained attribution is needed. SPEC-01 defines `IAddinMessage` types as only `tool_result`, `state_update`, `addin_ready`, `undo_group_outcome`, `addin_protocol_error`.
findings.problem: No teardown/disconnect message exists in the protocol, and a dropped WebSocket cannot distinguish graceful shutdown from crash/network loss. The closure reason taxonomy overclaims information the system cannot observe.
findings.why_it_matters: Audit closure reasons become inaccurate or non-implementable, which undermines the DHF session lifecycle semantics used elsewhere in the bundle.
findings.proposed_fix: Either add an explicit add-in teardown message to SPEC-01 with defined send conditions, or remove `explicit_shutdown` from the observable closure reasons until the protocol supports it.

findings.title: Viewer route contract conflicts between `/` and `/viewer`
findings.evidence: Migration matrix: `Viewer host | Same Railway service, path /viewer`. SPEC-06 §4.1 defines `GET /` as the viewer timeline root, and SPEC-06 §3 says the viewer registers endpoints on the orchestrator `WebApplication` with no separate listener.
findings.problem: The canonical public route for the viewer is defined two different ways.
findings.why_it_matters: This affects deployment, reverse-proxy rules, links, tests, and the threat model statements about what is publicly accessible. One side of the bundle will be wrong at runtime.
findings.proposed_fix: Choose one canonical viewer root (`/` or `/viewer`) and update SPEC-06, SPEC-00 references, and the migration document to match exactly.

top_3_must_fix: Remove unauthenticated tenant/session enumeration from the v1 viewer or the claimed URL-capability security model is false.
Define a concrete persisted recovery-event model and hash-chain integration; `AppendRecoveryEventAsync` is currently unimplementable.
Align screenshot storage with the schema and read contracts; deep validation and viewer rendering currently depend on data the DHF does not store.
